raw:
The task is to write app UI strings in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan usage) for a system settings screen showing an app list, with a button to completely remove an app from the device.

Requirements:
- s1: the button (to completely remove the app from the device)
- s2: confirmation dialog title
- s3: status text after completion

Taiwan usage: use 解除安裝 instead of 卸載.

Let me think about what Taiwan Android/system settings typically use:
- Uninstall button: "解除安裝"
- Confirmation dialog title: "解除安裝應用程式？" or "要解除安裝這個應用程式嗎？"
- Status after completion: "已解除安裝"

Taiwan UI conventions:
- "應用程式" for app
- Confirmation dialogs often phrased as "要...嗎？" or "是否..."
- Status text: "已解除安裝" is standard.

s1 could be just "解除安裝" (button labels are usually short). The description says "把它從裝置上完全移除的按鈕" — the button to completely remove it from the device. That's uninstall. So "解除安裝".

s2: "解除安裝應用程式？" — a common title format. Or "要解除安裝這個應用程式嗎？" Taiwan Android system dialogs sometimes say "要解除安裝這個應用程式嗎？" Actually in Android Taiwan Chinese, the uninstall confirmation is "要解除安裝這個應用程式嗎？" Hmm. Both work. For a title, concise: "解除安裝應用程式？"

s3: "已解除安裝" — status text after completion.

The user said only output a JSON object, keys s1, s2, s3, values strings, no other text.

Output:
{"s1": "解除安裝", "s2": "解除安裝應用程式？", "s3": "已解除安裝"}

Should I use full-width question mark? Taiwan UI typically uses "？" full-width. Yes.

JSON with Traditional Chinese characters is fine.</think>{"s1": "解除安裝", "s2": "解除安裝應用程式？", "s3": "已解除安裝"}
